title: RCMP cleared in death of Red Deer man shot amid mental health crisis
article: The father of a Red Deer man who was killed in an officer-involved shooting has been left outraged after the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team concluded "proportionate, necessary and reasonable" force was used.
ASIRT released a report on Thursday, Feb. 13 regarding the death of Derek Deon in April 2023.

"There are many inaccuracies in this report, but It comes as no surprise to me that ASIRT director has released this decision without the medical examiner's report in the midst of a complaint against the Lead ASSIRT investigator, the Executive Director and author of the ASIRT report himself as well as CCRC complaint against a RCMP officer in relation to ASSIRT lead complaint regarding interference in a criminal investigation and hearing," Vernon Deon, Derek's father said in an email statement.
Derek, who was diagnosed with a schizophrenia spectrum disorder, was in the midst of a mental health crisis on April 13, 2023 - his parents Jane and Vernon called 911 after Derek made verbal threats.

Three RCMP officers arrived at the family's home and were told Derek was in the basement. The officers found him laying on a mattress on the basement floor. According to an ASIRT report, the officers "repeatedly attempted to engage with" Derek and informed him that he was being apprehended under the Mental Health Act, but he "refused to comply or co-operate" with being taken into custody.

The officer who would later fire their service pistol approached Derek to place handcuffs on him and take him into custody, but saw him grab a knife from under his body as he began to sit up. The officer backed away, drew his Conducted Energy Weapon and, while pointing it at Derek, instructed him to drop the knife.

When Derek continued to hold the knife, the officer discharged the Conducted Energy Weapon, but it had "limited effect" and did not incapacitate Derek, states the ASIRT report. The officer then drew his firearm.

Another responding officer then discharged his Conducted Energy Weapon as well, "but it also did not have the desired effect." Derek was on his knees while still holding the knife. The ASIRT report claims Derek "lunged towards" the officer who had drew his firearm.
"Fearing for his and his fellow officers' safety, (subject officer) discharged his service pistol towards (Derek), striking him several times," states the report.
Additional officers responded to the home and despite administering first aid, Derek was declared deceased at the scene.
Derek's father, Vernon, was interviewed for the ASIRT report. He "expressed anger at the incident and the way the attending officers dealt with it," the report states.

"He described the incident as an assassination. He stated he was present in the basement and witnessed the interaction. (Vernon) described the officers 'Tasering' his son, which made his son go to his knees. He then saw his son, while holding a knife, move towards an officer. The officer then shot his son. (Vernon) stated that he did not hear the officer issue any warnings."

ASIRT states that under Section 25 of the Criminal Code, a police officer is justified in doing what he or she is authorized to do and to use as much force as is reasonably necessary where he or she has reasonable grounds to do so. (Force intended to cause death or grievous bodily harm is justified if the officer believes, on reasonable grounds, that the force was necessary to prevent the death or grievous bodily harm of the officer and/or any other person.)

"After a thorough, independent, and objective investigation into the conduct of the (subject officer), it is my opinion that he was lawfully placed, and acting properly in the execution of his duties," the report concluded.

"There is no evidence to support any belief that any officer engaged in any unlawful or unreasonable conduct that would give rise to an offence. While the death of (affected person) is unfortunate, the force used by (subject officer) was proportionate, necessary and reasonable in all the circumstances."
